paper_title: Analysis of the Structural Diversity, Substitution Patterns, and Frequency of Nitrogen Heterocycles among U.S. FDA Approved Pharmaceuticals
mechanistic_insights: The paper is a statistical analysis of existing drug structures, not a study of reaction mechanisms or optimization.
59% of unique small-molecule FDA-approved drugs contain a nitrogen heterocycle.
The most common nitrogen heterocycles in FDA-approved drugs are piperidine, pyridine, and piperazine.
Six-membered nitrogen heterocycles (found in 59% of N-heterocyclic drugs) are more prevalent than five-membered ones (39%).
The analysis reveals common substitution patterns for prevalent heterocycles, such as the preference for N1 and C4 substitution on piperidines.

quantitative_outcomes.notes: This paper is a review that provides a statistical analysis of the frequency and structural diversity of nitrogen heterocycles in FDA-approved drugs. It does not report on synthetic methods, reaction conditions, or yields. The quantitative data pertains to the count and prevalence of different chemical structures in pharmaceuticals.
